title: Monday · prime factorization, evidence and Nevermoor
arrival: Answer attendance, then hand in any forms. Get paper and a pencil ready.
note: Our four-day learning week: explain how you know. Friday October 23 is a non-instructional day. No inequalities upload is required. Continue Nevermoor from our actual bookmark. Provincial Student Vote is Thursday October 22; our voting slot is pending.

blocks.title: Arrival and attendance
studentSteps: Settle in and answer attendance.
Hand in any forms afterward.

blocks.title: Maths · prime factorization
blocks.notes: Math Antics Prime Factorization, then compare trees for 24 starting with 4 × 6 and 3 × 8. Practise 18, 30 and 36; challenge 60. Exit: prime-factorize 42, explain why finished, multiply back. Use paper and pencils; no counters or printing needed. Keep Pack It / Sync It for a later GCF lesson.
blocks.firstAction: Decide which of 2, 4, 7 and 9 are prime. Explain how you know.
studentSteps: Watch Math Antics and predict the next factor split.
Compare two trees for 24. Split until every end number is prime.
Prime-factorize 18, 30 and 36; try two trees for 60 if ready.
Independently prime-factorize 42, explain why you are finished, and multiply back.

activity.label: Prime factorization · video, trees and practice

blocks.title: Literacy · explain with evidence
blocks.notes: Model: Both trees for 24 end in 2 × 2 × 2 × 3. These end numbers are prime, and their product is 24. Students may instead explain an idea from a recently read text. Allow oral rehearsal, drawings, labels and scribing.
blocks.firstAction: Explain a factor tree or an idea from a text we have read.
studentSteps: Explain a factor tree or an idea from a text we have read.
Add one detail that supports your explanation.
Ask a partner to retell your idea, then improve one unclear sentence.

blocks.title: Snack
blocks.firstAction: Put your work away and have your snack.

blocks.title: Social studies · check our party posters
blocks.notes: Use posters already underway and original sources; give all parties equal attention. Model: The party proposes ___. Our source is ___. This could affect ___. Assess explanation, not political preference.
blocks.firstAction: Open your existing poster and check one proposal against its source.
studentSteps: Check your party name, leader and three provincial proposals against the original sources.
Distinguish the party leader from the local candidate. Record sources and clarify uncertain claims.
Explain one verified proposal in your own words to a partner.

blocks.title: Writing and maths workshop
blocks.notes: Revisit morning explanations and factor trees. Use the exit check to choose targeted practice or further reasoning. Keep repeated prime factors and check by multiplying back. Save the counter/GCF investigation for a later lesson.
blocks.firstAction: Bring your morning explanation or factor trees.
studentSteps: Bring your morning explanation or factor trees.
Practise the next step with your group or revise independently.
Show one example you can now explain on your own.

blocks.title: Lunch
blocks.notes: Usual intermediate routine: outside 11:50–12:12; transition 12:12–12:13; eating 12:13–12:35.
blocks.firstAction: Follow our outside-play and lunch routine.
blocks.firstActionKo: 바깥 놀이와 점심시간에는 정해진 순서대로 하세요.

blocks.title: Quiet individual time
blocks.notes: A calm reset with quiet non-reading choices.
blocks.firstAction: Choose quiet reading, drawing or an unfinished task.
studentSteps: Choose quiet reading, drawing or an unfinished task.

blocks.title: Work block · Career and Action Packs
blocks.notes: Finish existing learning; choose one manageable action and identify any adult help or materials needed.
blocks.firstAction: Choose an unfinished task or your next Action Pack step.
studentSteps: Choose an unfinished task or your next Action Pack step.
Make progress and mark where to continue.

blocks.title: English Language Arts · Nevermoor
blocks.notes: Reconstruct the last scene with two reliable details before listening on. Mark uncertainty instead of filling story gaps. Add one new idea/detail response and record the bookmark.
blocks.firstAction: Recall the last part we actually heard, or listen to the opening.
studentSteps: Listen for a character or setting detail.
Write, draw or say an idea and the detail that supports it.
Keep one question for our next reading.
blocks.firstActionKo: 지난번에 들은 마지막 부분을 떠올리거나 이야기의 시작 부분을 들으세요.

blocks.title: Finish and reflect
studentSteps: Save or organize your work.
Name one thing you can explain better now.

blocks.title: Planners, jobs and cleanup
blocks.notes: Keep routine cleanup around 2:00; move unfinished learning forward.
blocks.firstAction: Restore our room and record any confirmed reminders.
blocks.firstActionKo: 교실을 정리하고 확정된 안내 사항을 적으세요.

blocks.title: Classroom community
blocks.notes: Use a short check-in, appreciation or familiar cooperative game. Students may speak, draw, point or pass; keep feedback specific and avoid public rankings.
blocks.firstAction: Notice one helpful action from today.
studentSteps: Offer one specific appreciation or listen.
Name a small next step for tomorrow.
blocks.firstActionKo: 오늘 도움이 된 행동 한 가지를 떠올려 보세요.

blocks.title: Pack up and dismissal
blocks.firstAction: Check your belongings and get ready for a calm departure.
blocks.firstActionKo: 자기 물건을 확인하고 차분히 하교할 준비를 하세요.

backups: Use the on-page factor-tree model or draw both trees for 24 on the board if the video is unavailable. Paper and pencils are enough.
Use printed poster sources; record unanswered questions instead of guessing.
Carry unfinished learning into the next suitable work block.
